A deceased predecessor’s grant precedes Cheng’s accession in Taining 3, supporting the inclusive upper bound AD 325 without identifying the predecessor as Ming. Approval is source-approach only, not date, chapter, or publication approval.

Ming is the natural immediate-predecessor reading of 先帝 during Cheng’s reign; Yuan or a general recollection of earlier imperial patronage remains possible. Every such reading fits on or before AD 325. No exact grant year, lower endpoint, reign-span activity, or canonical identity is established. The 340-341 correspondence context and the separate unresolved Goguryeo chronology do not date this earlier grant. Approval is source-approach only, not date, chapter, or publication approval.

It does not imply continuous activity throughout a reign, that the former emperor was alive during the later letter, or identification with Ming. It supplies no unsupported lower endpoint or exact grant date. Approval is source-approach only, not date, chapter, or publication approval.

references.reason: Complete volume 006 records Ming’s testament for his son Yan and Ming’s death under Taining 3 (AD 325). Its linked continuation, volume 007, explicitly states 閏月戊子，明帝崩。己丑，太子卽皇帝位 under Cheng. The host’s short quotation alone does not state accession; the complete passage and linked continuation establish the succession endpoint. Volume 006 critical note 17 concerns an impossible February cyclical day and volume 007 note 1 concerns September entry order; neither challenges this year-level endpoint. All supplied Chinese and English source units and contextual claims were reviewed; the chapter 109 documents establish grant ownership and the current emperor’s context. This source-approach approval does not release the native candidate from its hold before a fresh full date audit.
